terms: ## Conversational Texture The user explicitly asked to avoid arbitrary optimization and only fix real correctness or workflow issues. This story should therefore deliver measurable duplicate-work reduction while preserving the Proofbound host-neutral evidence model and stale-proof guarantees.

## Key Insights The useful idea is not fountain-code redundancy and not mtime-based caching. Proofbound evidence must remain exact and hash-bound, so the safe primitive is a command-local snapshot tied to HEAD plus worktree/index dirtiness and material-scope semantics.

## Solution Tradeoffs Keep the change narrow: reuse a captured hash binding inside a single command or gate run, then prove invalidation when git state changes. Avoid global cache, streaming rewrites, parallel execution changes, or research harness changes in this story.

## Trigger Event On 2026-06-30, the DNAcoder transfer analysis identified syndrome-style short-circuiting as the one optimization idea that maps to a real Proofbound pain point: repeated materialHash and storyFilesHash recomputation across DONE and review gates.

This story should therefore deliver measurable duplicate-work reduction while preserving the Proofbound host-neutral evidence model and stale-proof guarantees.

Introduce a narrow command-local freshness snapshot so DONE and review assurance gates can reuse one authoritative HEAD/material/story-files binding within the same command execution. This is not a global cache and must not weaken stale-evidence detection; it only removes duplicate whole-tree hash recomputation after the binding has already been captured for the same git state.
